classification.difficultyReason: Use two right triangles sharing the building height, then round the depression angle to the nearest minute.

content.prompt:
Calculate the angle of depression from the top of the building to the car.

Answer to the nearest minute.

spec.description: Outline building and car on horizontal ground, with A to the left, dashed sight lines to the two top corners, a 38-degree angle at A, 25 m and 62 m horizontal dimensions, both base right-angle markers and the not-to-scale notice. Coordinates are illustrative, not physical measurements.
spec.mathematics: The common building height is 25 tan(38 degrees). The car is 62 m horizontally from the right base. The unknown depression angle equals the elevation angle at the car.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no height or depression-angle answer is printed.

answer.worked:
Let $h$ metres be the building height and $\theta$ the angle of depression. The angle of elevation at the car equals $\theta$ because the horizontal lines are parallel.

$$\begin{align*}\tan 38^{\circ} &= \frac{h}{25}\\h &= 25\tan 38^{\circ}\\\tan\theta &= \frac{25\tan 38^{\circ}}{62}\\\theta &= \tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{25\tan 38^{\circ}}{62}\right)\\\theta &\approx 17^{\circ}29'\end{align*}$$
